symptom: An intermediate research-only GitHub contents write emitted doubled backslashes inside a TypeScript regular-expression literal. Official CI research-governance typecheck failed with TS1127/TS1134/TS1135/TS1005, and verify test execution reported 14 transform failures. The exact source was read back and corrected before the next material attempt; no research data or runner failure was involved.
lesson: When authoring regex literals through a JavaScript template string, source-level backslashes can be doubled before GitHub writes the file. Readback of exact emitted characters and compiler diagnostics is necessary; retries of unchanged source cannot resolve a parse error.
guardrail: Construct regex source with String.raw or an explicitly verified single-escape representation; read back exact emitted source and inspect character counts before relying on CI. On red CI, separate parser/typecheck and test-transform exits from workflow conclusion and successful post-job cleanup. Reuse earlier generated-source escaping guardrails, repair the material source, and never rerun protected N2 for diagnostics.
